# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-17 (Extended v133)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 5—Louis Philippe's reign)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Rue de la Verrerie (Courfeyrac's residence); Rue Plumet (Valjean's house); Rue de l'Homme Armé (Valjean's apartment); Rue de l'Ouest (Valjean's apartment); Faubourg Saint-Antoine; Faubourg Saint-Marceau; wine-shops (Seven Billiards on Rue des Mathurins-Saint-Jacques; Corinthe on Rue Mondétour; Richefeu's at Barrière du Maine; Café Musain); schools; Boulevard de l'Hôpital; Jardin des Plantes; English provincial towns (Dunstead harbor town, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt, Quenford). **Environmental details**: Frost silvered hedges overnight; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; rain threatened; wind carries salt/tar scent; bees hum in lavender; children chase hoop down lane; road ruts and puddles after thaw; smoke from chimneys lies flat; gulls quarrel over fish heads; bells ring for vespers; light goes early; river up in spring; baker's boy often late; lines at oven grow long. Dogs bark at nothing. Clouds predicted rain, wrongly.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, charcoal sketches, moisture. Fireplace with red-hot brazier. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo**: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy). Rope-ladder with hooks, verdigris candlestick.

**RUE PLUMET HOUSE (Valjean's residence, October 1829-present)**: Originally built mid-last-century by Paris Parliament chief justice as secret mistress-house in deserted Rue Blomet (now Rue Plumet), near Combat des Animaux. Single-story pavilion: two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic under roof. Garden about one-and-a-half acres with large street gate. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms and cellar) for concealing child/nurse. Building communicates via masked secret-spring door to long narrow paved winding corridor (open sky, hemmed by lofty walls, hidden between garden enclosures and cultivated land), ending quarter-league distant at Rue du Babylone with another secret-lock door. Chief justice used passage to reach Rue de Babylone undetected. In 1793, coppersmith purchased house intending demolition but went bankrupt; house remained uninhabited, furnished with old furniture, slowly ruined. Yellow illegible notice on garden wall since 1819. October 1829: Valjean (as M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman) hired house as-is with back building and lane; repaired secret door openings, replaced paving-stones in courtyard, bricks in floors, steps in stairs, missing inlaid floor bits, lattice window glass. No gossiping neighbors—none existed. Valjean installed with Cosette and elderly maid Toussaint (rescued from hospital/wretchedness; stammerer from provinces).

**VALJEAN'S OTHER APARTMENTS**: Rue de l'Homme Armé (poor appearance); Rue de l'Ouest (poor appearance). Both remote from each other and Rue Plumet. Strategy: rotate residence monthly/six-weeks, served by porters, posing as gentleman from suburbs with temporary resting-place in town.

**WINE-SHOPS & MEETING PLACES**: Centers of revolutionary fermentation. **Seven Billiards (Rue des Mathurins-Saint-Jacques)** and **Café Rue Saint-Hyacinthe**: student rallying points. **Corinthe (Rue Mondétour)**: young men assemble; secret and public meetings. **Richefeu's (Barrière du Maine)**: marble-workers, painters, journeymen sculptors meet 12-1 o'clock. **Café Musain**: Société des Amis de l'A B C affiliated to Mutualists and Cougourde of Aix.

**M. MABEUF'S ESTABLISHMENTS**: Garden at Austerlitz (bad exposure, only shade/damp plants); Jardin des Plantes corner (good exposure for indigo trials, at his own expense).

**PRISONS**: La Force (Bâtiment-Neuf or court Saint-Bernard; robbers call it Fosse-aux-Lions; wall covered with scales, leprosy; old rusty iron door to ancient chapel; dormitories for ruffians; Charlemagne courtyard with sutler's window; fever ward with twenty-eight beds). Les Madelonettes. Salpêtrière.

## Marius Pontmercy: Psychological and Financial Crisis
**Identity and background**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's instruction regarding Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Recognized Thénardier in Waterloo painting.

**The Ambush Crisis (resolved with escape)**: Jondrette/Thénardier plotted extortion via Cosette. M. Leblanc escaped: unscrewed coin piece, used as saw to cut cords, brandished red-hot chisel above head emitting threatening glow. **While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty.** Dashed from window. Javert positioned outside with men; took action before Marius's signal. Thénardier woman hurled enormous paving-stone at Javert's head; Javert ducked; stone struck wall. Javert bore off prisoners in three hackney-coaches.

**Marius's aftermath (April Year 4)**: Relocated to Courfeyrac at Rue de la Verrerie for political reasons; paid quarterly rent, vacated hovel. Two reasons: (1) horror of wicked poor man development; (2) avoid lawsuit testimony against Thénardier. Recognized M. Leblanc as Monsieur Fabre (Cosette's biological father). Cosette believed Valjean her father, became convent scholar.

**Current financial crisis (Spring Year 5)**: **First time in life, Marius borrowed five francs from Courfeyrac; now borrows hundred-sou piece (five francs).** Poverty returned; felt icy breath. Discontinued work—dangerous habit vanishing, difficult to resume. Old coat becoming impossible; new coat growing old; shirts wearing out; hat wearing out; boots giving out.

**Work situation**: Task consists of turning into French celebrated quarrel between Germans, the Gans and Savigny controversy. Cannot focus: reads four lines, attempts to write one, sees star between himself and paper, abandons task.

**Psychological state—Reverie vs. Reason**: Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working and moving firmly toward fixed goal, but endowed with more clear-sightedness and rectitude than ever. Judgment almost wholly disassociated from hope. Meditation turns to reproach; reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining on him, night growing more dense. **No longer even sees the sun.** Yet sensations reach him: laundresses of Gobelins beating linen, birds chattering in elm-trees—sounds of liberty and toil cause him to meditate deeply. **Happy, even in midst of anguish, is he to whom God has given a soul worthy of love and of unhappiness!**

**Marius and Cosette relationship—Memory and hope**: She—that was Marius's whole thought. One sweet idea alone left: she had loved him; her glance told him so; she did not know his name, but she knew his soul. Pure, impersonal, ideal reveries fell upon notebook. He called this "writing to her." **Periodical five francs a double riddle**: to Courfeyrac who lent, to unknown recipient who received them. Continues dreaming of "Her."

**Éponine's approach (Spring Year 5)**: Encountered Marius on riverside. **She had grown poorer and prettier—double progress towards light and distress. Barefooted and in rags, holes larger, tatters more sordid than two months prior.** She inquired where he lived now (having been jailed fortnight, released—not yet at years of discretion). Revealed she hunted six weeks for him; Father Mabeuf had directed her. Mocked his old hat, called him Baron Marius. Questioned his residence change from Gorbeau house.

## M. Mabeuf: Decline and Hope
**Status (Spring Year 5)**: Nearly eighty years old. Health declining; old servant Mother Plutarque ill and in bed (unpaid wages for fifteen months). Subsists on minimal diet: breakfast reduced to two eggs, leaves one for servant; often his only meal. No longer smiles infantile smile; grown morose; no longer receives visitors. Passes Marius sometimes on Boulevard de l'Hôpital; exchange only melancholy sign of head. **"A heart-breaking thing it is that there comes a moment when misery looses bonds! Two men who have been friends become two chance passers-by."**

**_Flora of Cauteretz_ project**: Book no longer sells at all. Experiments on indigo unsuccessful in Austerlitz garden (bad exposure). Pawned copperplates of _Flora_ to obtain corner in Jardin des Plantes with good exposure for indigo trials at his own expense.

**Mabeuf's three forms of happiness**: His books, his garden, his indigo. Plans: "When I shall have made my balls of blueing, I shall be rich, I will withdraw my copperplates from pawn-shop, put my _Flora_ in vogue again with trickery, plenty of money and advertisements in newspapers and I will buy, I know well where, a copy of Pierre de Médine's _Art de Navigier_, with wood-cuts, edition of 1655."

**Daily routine**: Toils all day over indigo plot; at night returns home to water his garden and read his books.

**Mysterious visitor (early Spring Year 5)**: While sitting on overturned stone post in garden at broad daylight, emerged "a sort of tall, slender girl, who drew herself up in front of him and stared boldly at him. She had less the air of a human being than of a form which had just blossomed forth from the twilight." Unhooked well-chain, plunged in and withdrew bucket, filled watering-pot, ran barefooted in tattered petticoat among flower-beds distributing water. **"The sound of the watering-pot on the leaves filled Father Mabeuf's soul with ecstasy."** As he fell asleep, bewildered: "it came back to him."

## Jean Valjean and Cosette: New Residence (October 1829-present)
**Valjean's decision and justification**: Recognized necessity of leaving convent after five years. Anguish at requiring Cosette's departure, but concluded danger to him alone insufficient to condemn her to cloister. Decided to be prudent; take precautions. Resolved to adopt false identity and multiple residences to avoid recapture by Javert.

**Convent departure**: Demanded audience with Reverend Prioress; fabricated story of inheritance from deceased brother permitting life without working. Offered five thousand francs to community as indemnity for Cosette's five years free education (since she took no vows).

**Current residence strategy**: Primary residence Rue Plumet (Valjean as M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman). Two secondary apartments (Rue de l'Homme Armé, Rue de l'Ouest) for rotating monthly/six-week stays to attract less attention, enable rapid escape if necessary, avoid being caught unprovided as on Javert-escape night. Servants: Toussaint (elderly, stammering, provincial) at Rue Plumet; porters at other apartments serve him, presenting himself as gentleman from suburbs.

**Cosette**: Now living with Valjean at Rue Plumet. Her biological father Monsieur Fabre (M. Leblanc) remains unaware of her location; she continues believing Valjean her father.

## Enjolras and Revolutionary Leadership (Spring Year 5)
**Enjolras as nexus of fermentation**: Believed moment at hand: people taking possession of right; revolution majestically taking France. Furnace being heated. Had powder train of friends scattered all over Paris.

**Composed network**: Collaborators include Combeferre (philosophical, penetrating eloquence), Feuilly (cosmopolitan enthusiasm), Courfeyrac (dash), Bahorel (smile), Jean Prouvaire (melancholy), Joly (science), Bossuet (sarcasms). Created sort of electric spark taking fire nearly everywhere.

## Revolutionary Fermentation and Secret Societies (Spring Year 5)
**Public agitation and cartridge-making (April Year 4)**: Workmen openly proclaim cartridge-making. Police raids: April 5, arrested Pardon while preparing cartridges. Weapons transfer documented.

**Discovered documents**: Package on bench near Austerlitz bridge: printed dialogues, song "Workmen, band together," tin box full cartridges. Ditch between Père-Lachaise and Barrière du Trône: bag with bullet-mould, wooden punch, wooden bowl with hunting-powder grains, cast-iron pot with melted lead traces. **Carpenter found cipher document**: Q, C, D, E with instruction "Learn this list by heart." Letters meant quinturions, centurions, decurions, éclaireurs; date u og a' fe = April 15, Year 4.

**Secret society network**: Associations of Friends of People → Society of Rights of Man → Society of Action (impatient individuals breaking away). Other associations: Gallic Society; committee of organization of Municipalities; associations for liberty of press, individual liberty, instruction against indirect taxes; Society of Equal Workingmen (levellers, communists, reformers); Army of Bastilles.

**Military infiltration**: Counted on: fifty-second regiment, fifth, eighth, thirty-seventh, twentieth light cavalry. Burgundy and southern towns: planted liberty trees. Network spreading like membranes.

## Javert's Outstanding Question and Prison Intelligence Operations
**After M. Leblanc's escape (April Year 4)**: Javert did not take prisoner prisoner. **"The assassinated man who flees is more suspicious than the assassin."** M. Leblanc's identity and whereabouts remain mystery.

**Patron Minette gang members**: Captured: Babet, Gueulemer. Released: Éponine, Azelma (Les Madelonettes). Montparnasse encountered Éponine, preferred to play Nemorin with daughter rather than Schinderhannes with father. Three prowlers (Kruideniers/Bizarro, Glorieux, Barre-Carosse) captured late Year 4.

**Brujon's operations (Late Year 4 through February Year 5)**: Long-haired man of Rue du Petit-Banquier; La Force souvenir. Released in Charlemagne courtyard. Feigned fever, inquired about fever ward. End February Year 5: executed three commissions for fifty sous (Panthéon 10 sous, Val-de-Grâce 15 sous, Barrière de Grenelle 25 sous)—homes of three prowlers. Week after discovery: night inspection found Brujon writing by hall-lamp light; placed solitary month. Note not seized.

**Prison communication**: "Postilion"—moulded bread pallet sent over roofs courtyard-to-courtyard with notes. Babet passed note La Force to Salpêtrière to good friend. Woman transmitted to Magnon (suspected, not arrested), who bridged Salpêtrière and Les Madelonettes via Éponine.

**Éponine's reconnaissance (Year 5)**: Released Les Madelonettes. Magnon handed her Brujon's note. Went to Rue Plumet, recognized gate and garden, observed house, spied, lurked. Brought biscuit (prison "nothing to be done" symbol) to Magnon, transmitted to Babet's Salpêtrière mistress.

## English Provincial Towns: Population and Daily Life (Documented)
**Movement and relationships**: Peten Haskick moved to Quenford; Lura Haskick followed. Kadrek moved to Wilholt. Zalis Corrley's daughter settled Wilholt. Kadan Corrley married Yewyn Corrford at Kelmere. Quiet Jotho married Fewyn Stenworth's eldest at Ostcombe; couple lived there. **Nelan died of coughing sickness; buried Kelford.** **Taric Corrley quit Kelmere, lodged Staveford. Kassa Stenson moved Staveford.** **Ulrald Corrford apprenticed, became smith; gave bone compass to Fenelle Lindmere.** **Son born to Yewyn Haskick and Tatho Brackick; called Semor Brackick; family lives Ravenmere.** **Matho found work Dungate, moved there, not returned Yarlby.** **Fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose (revealed by Ismira Stenson in letter youngest Nelan Brackick burned).** Families: Stenworth, Prydenridge, Thornmere, Lindmere, Brackick, Stenenridge, Corrford, Haskick.

**Daily mundane activities**: Sorting old letters by candlelight. Mending torn sleeves by window. Scrubbing steps while humming. **Yewyn Haskick complained of aching back, as usual.** **Yewyn gave Tatho solemn promise to pay old Stenworth debt.** Salt price scandal debated. Coins counted, penny short. Ribbon bought, regretted. Weather, harvest, river constant. **Yewyn and Rorald talked nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse.** Yewyn read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. **Pelia and Yewyn watched clouds, predicted rain, wrongly.** Children chased hoop shrieking. Argued over oat sack price. Walked long way round muddy square.

## Louis Philippe and Historical Context
**Louis Philippe (Spring Year 5)**: Handsome in old age, graceful. Lacked majesty; wore no crown, no white hair. Mixture of noble and bourgeois suited 1830. Incorruptible; went out with umbrella. Policy domestic rather than national; excessive timidity displeasing to people. Press free, tribune free, conscience and speech free. **Will remain one of best princes who ever sat on throne.** Cloud gathering—strange shade from wraths and systems. Everything hastily stifled, moving, fermenting. Electric tension such that first comer brought light. Petty revolts suppressed but ever bursting afresh—sign of vast underlying conflagration.
